title: Public Service Rules & Code of Conduct
objective: Equip officers with a working knowledge of the Public Service Rules, the Code of Conduct for public officers, and the standards of behaviour expected in government service.
description: A practical introduction to the rules that govern appointment, conduct, discipline and accountability in the public service, with real-world scenarios on gifts, conflict of interest and asset declaration.

lessons.title: Introduction to the Public Service Rules
lessons.description: The Public Service Rules (PSR) set out the conditions of service for federal public officers: appointment, confirmation, promotion, leave, discipline and retirement. This lesson walks through how the PSR is structured, how it relates to circulars issued by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, and where officers can find the provisions that apply to them.

questions.question: Which document primarily regulates the conditions of service of federal public servants?
options: The Companies and Allied Matters Act
questions.answer: The Public Service Rules

questions.question: Which body is responsible for receiving and verifying asset declarations by public officers?
questions.answer: Code of Conduct Bureau

questions.question: When are public officers expected to declare their assets?
options: On assumption of office, periodically while in office, and at the end of tenure
Only when requested by a journalist
questions.answer: On assumption of office, periodically while in office, and at the end of tenure

lessons.title: Conflict of Interest, Gifts & Hospitality
lessons.description: A conflict of interest arises when an officer's private interests could improperly influence the performance of official duties. This lesson covers how to recognise conflicts, how to declare them, and how to handle gifts and hospitality from contractors, vendors and members of the public.

questions.question: A contractor offers you an expensive gift while their bid is under evaluation. What should you do?
options: Decline the gift and report the offer through the appropriate channel
Accept it quietly since it is a personal gift
Accept it and share it with colleagues
Accept it after the contract is awarded
questions.answer: Decline the gift and report the offer through the appropriate channel

questions.question: A conflict of interest exists when...
options: Personal interests could improperly influence official decisions
Two departments disagree on a budget
A staff member requests annual leave
questions.answer: Personal interests could improperly influence official decisions

questions.question: You discover a relative owns a company bidding for a contract you are evaluating. What is the correct action?
options: Declare the interest and recuse yourself from the evaluation
Continue but score the company fairly
Tell the relative to lower their price
questions.answer: Declare the interest and recuse yourself from the evaluation

lessons.title: Discipline, Misconduct & Fair Hearing
lessons.description: This lesson explains the difference between general and serious misconduct, the disciplinary process (query, response, panel review and sanction), and the principle of fair hearing that protects every officer.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally treated as serious misconduct?
questions.answer: Falsification of official records

questions.question: Before a disciplinary sanction is applied, the officer should be...
options: Issued a query and given an opportunity to respond
questions.answer: Issued a query and given an opportunity to respond

questions.question: The principle that every officer must be heard before being sanctioned is called...
questions.answer: Fair hearing

title: Public Procurement Fundamentals
objective: Enable officers involved in buying goods, works and services to follow the Public Procurement Act 2007 and achieve value for money with transparency.
description: Covers the legal framework for public procurement, procurement methods, approval thresholds, the role of the Bureau of Public Procurement, and contract management and record keeping.

lessons.title: Principles & Legal Framework of Public Procurement
lessons.description: Public procurement at the federal level is governed by the Public Procurement Act 2007, which established the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP). This lesson introduces the core principles of value for money, competition, transparency, accountability and fairness.

questions.question: Which law governs public procurement at the federal level in Nigeria?
questions.answer: Public Procurement Act 2007

questions.question: Which body regulates and monitors federal public procurement?
questions.answer: Bureau of Public Procurement

questions.question: Which of these is a core principle of public procurement?
questions.answer: Value for money

lessons.title: Procurement Methods & Approvals
lessons.description: Open competitive bidding is the default method for public procurement. Other methods, such as selective tendering, request for quotations and direct procurement, are allowed only in justified circumstances. This lesson explains when each method applies and how approval thresholds and the Certificate of No Objection work.

questions.question: What is the default procurement method for large public contracts?
options: Direct award to a known vendor
questions.answer: Open competitive bidding

questions.question: Direct procurement may be used...
options: Only in justified and documented exceptional circumstances
When the vendor is a friend
For every contract below any amount
questions.answer: Only in justified and documented exceptional circumstances

questions.question: Splitting a contract into smaller parts to avoid approval thresholds is...
questions.answer: Prohibited

lessons.title: Contract Management & Record Keeping
lessons.description: Procurement does not end at contract award. This lesson covers monitoring delivery, handling contract variations, certifying completion, and keeping a complete procurement file as an audit trail.

questions.question: Why must complete procurement records be kept?
options: To provide an audit trail and ensure accountability
They are not necessary after payment
questions.answer: To provide an audit trail and ensure accountability

questions.question: A contract variation should be...
options: Justified, documented and approved by the appropriate authority
questions.answer: Justified, documented and approved by the appropriate authority

questions.question: Before payment is made for works, what should be confirmed?
options: That the works were delivered and certified as meeting specifications
That the vendor has asked twice
That the budget year is ending
questions.answer: That the works were delivered and certified as meeting specifications

questions.question: What does BPP stand for?
questions.answer: Bureau of Public Procurement

questions.question: Which method promotes the widest competition among bidders?
questions.answer: Open competitive bidding

questions.question: Which document gives approval to proceed with an award above certain thresholds?
questions.answer: Certificate of No Objection

questions.question: An evaluator with a personal interest in a bidder should...
options: Share bid details with the bidder
questions.answer: Declare it and step aside

questions.question: The main goal of public procurement is...
options: Achieving value for money for government
questions.answer: Achieving value for money for government

title: Data Protection & Cybersecurity Awareness
objective: Help every staff member protect personal data and official information, and recognise and report common cyber threats.
description: An awareness course on the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, safe handling of personal and official data, phishing and social engineering, passwords and incident reporting.

lessons.title: Personal Data & the Nigeria Data Protection Act
lessons.description: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 sets out how personal data must be collected, processed, stored and shared, and established the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC). This lesson explains what counts as personal data and the principles of lawful, fair and secure processing.

questions.question: What is Nigeria's primary data protection law?
questions.answer: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023

questions.question: Which body regulates data protection in Nigeria?
questions.answer: Nigeria Data Protection Commission

questions.question: Which of these is personal data?
options: A staff member's phone number and home address
The name of a public holiday
questions.answer: A staff member's phone number and home address

lessons.title: Phishing & Social Engineering
lessons.description: Most cyber incidents start with a human being tricked. This lesson shows how to spot phishing emails, fake calls and suspicious links, and what to do when you receive one.

questions.question: You get an email from 'IT Support' asking you to confirm your password through a link. What should you do?
options: Don't click, and report it to the IT/security team
Click the link and confirm quickly
questions.answer: Don't click, and report it to the IT/security team

questions.question: Which is a common sign of a phishing email?
options: Urgent tone and a sender address that doesn't match the organisation
An email sent during work hours
A message from your known supervisor's verified address
questions.answer: Urgent tone and a sender address that doesn't match the organisation

questions.question: What is the best practice for passwords?
options: Use a long, unique passphrase for each account and enable multi-factor authentication
Write it on a sticky note on your monitor
Share it with a trusted colleague
questions.answer: Use a long, unique passphrase for each account and enable multi-factor authentication

lessons.title: Handling Official Information & Reporting Incidents
lessons.description: Good security habits protect the organisation every day: locking your screen, using approved channels to share documents, classifying information correctly and reporting incidents quickly.

questions.question: You need to step away from your computer. What should you do?
options: Leave it open for a colleague
Nothing, it's fine for a few minutes
questions.answer: Lock your screen

questions.question: How should official documents be shared?
options: Through approved official channels and systems
On unencrypted USB drives left on desks
questions.answer: Through approved official channels and systems

questions.question: You suspect a data breach. What is the right first step?
options: Report it immediately to the designated officer or IT security
Wait to see if it happens again
questions.answer: Report it immediately to the designated officer or IT security

title: Effective Official Communication & Memo Writing
objective: Improve the clarity, tone and structure of official memos, letters, minutes, emails and presentations.
description: A hands-on course on writing for government and corporate audiences: structuring memos, recording minutes, email etiquette and presenting information persuasively.

lessons.title: Principles of Official Writing
lessons.description: Official writing should be clear, concise, correct and courteous. This lesson covers knowing your audience, putting the key message first, choosing a formal but readable tone, and avoiding unnecessary jargon.

questions.question: What is the most important quality of official writing?
questions.answer: Clarity and conciseness

questions.question: Where should the main message of a memo appear?
options: It should not be stated directly
questions.answer: Early, near the beginning

questions.question: What tone is appropriate for official correspondence?
questions.answer: Formal and courteous

lessons.title: Writing Memos & Minutes
lessons.description: This lesson breaks down the parts of a memo (reference, date, subject, body and action required) and shows how to write minutes that capture decisions, action points, owners and deadlines.

questions.question: A memo's subject line should...
options: State the purpose briefly and specifically
questions.answer: State the purpose briefly and specifically

questions.question: Good meeting minutes should record...
options: Decisions, action points, owners and deadlines
questions.answer: Decisions, action points, owners and deadlines

questions.question: Why do official memos carry reference numbers?
options: To make tracking and filing easier
questions.answer: To make tracking and filing easier

lessons.title: Email Etiquette & Presentations
lessons.description: Email and slide presentations are now the main ways we communicate at work. This lesson covers subject lines, reply-all discipline, attachments, proofreading and designing slides that support, rather than replace, the speaker.

questions.question: When should you use 'Reply All'?
options: Only when every recipient needs your response
questions.answer: Only when every recipient needs your response

questions.question: A good presentation slide has...
options: A few key points and supporting visuals
questions.answer: A few key points and supporting visuals

questions.question: What should you always do before sending an important email?
options: Proofread it and check the recipients and attachments
questions.answer: Proofread it and check the recipients and attachments

title: Leadership & People Management for Supervisors
objective: Prepare new and current supervisors to lead teams, delegate effectively, motivate staff and handle conflict professionally.
description: Practical leadership skills for unit heads and team leads in government agencies and corporate organisations: the supervisor's role, delegation, motivation, feedback and conflict resolution.

lessons.title: The Role of a Supervisor
lessons.description: Supervisors connect organisational goals to daily work. This lesson covers planning and assigning work, setting expectations, monitoring performance and serving as a role model for integrity and discipline.

questions.question: What is a supervisor's primary responsibility?
options: Guiding the team to achieve organisational goals
questions.answer: Guiding the team to achieve organisational goals

questions.question: Clear expectations help staff to...
options: Understand what success looks like in their role
questions.answer: Understand what success looks like in their role

questions.question: A supervisor who leads by example...
options: Demonstrates the behaviour they expect from the team
Sets rules that apply only to others
questions.answer: Demonstrates the behaviour they expect from the team

lessons.title: Delegation & Motivation
lessons.description: Delegation develops staff and frees the supervisor to focus on priorities. This lesson covers what to delegate, how to brief, how to follow up without micromanaging, and what motivates people at work.

questions.question: Effective delegation includes...
options: Clear instructions, authority to act and agreed check-ins
Taking the task back at the first mistake
questions.answer: Clear instructions, authority to act and agreed check-ins

questions.question: Which is a strong non-financial motivator?
questions.answer: Recognition and opportunities for growth

questions.question: Micromanagement usually leads to...
questions.answer: Lower morale and reduced initiative

lessons.title: Feedback & Conflict Resolution
lessons.description: Timely, specific feedback improves performance. This lesson introduces a simple feedback model (situation, behaviour, impact) and steps to resolve team conflicts fairly and early.

questions.question: Good feedback is...
options: Specific, timely and focused on behaviour
questions.answer: Specific, timely and focused on behaviour

questions.question: When two team members are in conflict, the supervisor should first...
options: Listen to both sides privately and identify the issue
Ignore it until it goes away
questions.answer: Listen to both sides privately and identify the issue

questions.question: In the Situation-Behaviour-Impact model, 'Impact' describes...
options: The effect the behaviour had on work or people
questions.answer: The effect the behaviour had on work or people

title: Performance Management & Appraisal
objective: Help staff and supervisors set SMART objectives, track performance throughout the year and conduct fair, evidence-based appraisals.
description: Covers the full performance cycle: goal setting, continuous feedback, documentation, the appraisal interview and development planning, aligned with annual performance evaluation practice in the public service.

lessons.title: Setting SMART Objectives
lessons.description: Objectives should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. This lesson shows how to turn departmental targets into individual SMART objectives agreed at the start of the performance cycle.

questions.question: What does the 'M' in SMART stand for?
questions.answer: Measurable

questions.question: Which objective is SMART?
options: Process 95% of leave requests within 3 working days by 31 December
questions.answer: Process 95% of leave requests within 3 working days by 31 December

questions.question: When should individual objectives be agreed?
options: At the start of the performance cycle
On the day of the appraisal
questions.answer: At the start of the performance cycle

lessons.title: Continuous Feedback & Documentation
lessons.description: Appraisal should never be a surprise. This lesson covers regular check-ins, mid-year reviews and keeping evidence of achievements and challenges throughout the year.

questions.question: Why hold regular performance check-ins?
options: To track progress and address issues early
To replace the annual appraisal entirely
questions.answer: To track progress and address issues early

questions.question: What should be documented during the year?
questions.answer: Achievements, challenges and supporting evidence

questions.question: A mid-year review is used to...
options: Review progress and adjust objectives if needed
questions.answer: Review progress and adjust objectives if needed

lessons.title: The Appraisal Interview & Development Plans
lessons.description: This lesson explains how to prepare for and conduct a fair appraisal interview, avoid common rating biases, and agree a development plan for the next cycle.

questions.question: Ratings in an appraisal should be based on...
options: Evidence of performance against agreed objectives
questions.answer: Evidence of performance against agreed objectives

questions.question: Rating someone highly on everything because they excel in one area is called...
questions.answer: The halo effect

questions.question: A development plan should include...
options: Specific training or experiences to close skill gaps
questions.answer: Specific training or experiences to close skill gaps

title: Customer Service Excellence & SERVICOM
objective: Build a citizen- and customer-focused service culture in line with SERVICOM principles.
description: Explores service standards, the SERVICOM charter, handling complaints, communicating with stakeholders and continuously improving service delivery.

lessons.title: Understanding SERVICOM & Service Charters
lessons.description: SERVICOM (Service Compact with All Nigerians) commits government agencies to deliver services that are timely, fair, honest, effective and transparent. This lesson explains service charters, published service standards, and the role of SERVICOM units in agencies.

questions.question: What does SERVICOM stand for?
questions.answer: Service Compact with All Nigerians

questions.question: A service charter tells customers...
options: What services to expect, the standards, and how to complain
questions.answer: What services to expect, the standards, and how to complain

questions.question: Which value is central to good public service delivery?
questions.answer: Timeliness and fairness

lessons.title: Handling Complaints & Difficult Customers
lessons.description: Complaints are free feedback. This lesson covers active listening, empathy, staying calm, taking ownership and following through to resolution and record keeping.

questions.question: What is the first step when handling a complaint?
options: Listen actively and acknowledge the concern
questions.answer: Listen actively and acknowledge the concern

questions.question: When you can't resolve an issue yourself, you should...
options: Escalate it, tell the customer the next steps, and follow up
Tell the customer it's not your job
questions.answer: Escalate it, tell the customer the next steps, and follow up

questions.question: Why should complaints be recorded?
options: To track resolution and identify recurring problems
questions.answer: To track resolution and identify recurring problems

lessons.title: Continuous Service Improvement
lessons.description: Excellent organisations measure service, ask customers for feedback and fix root causes. This lesson introduces simple service metrics and improvement cycles.

questions.question: Which is a useful service metric?
options: Average time taken to resolve a request
questions.answer: Average time taken to resolve a request

questions.question: Customer feedback should be used to...
options: Identify and fix root causes of poor service
Fill a report that nobody reads
questions.answer: Identify and fix root causes of poor service

questions.question: Continuous improvement means...
options: Regularly reviewing and improving how services are delivered
Changing nothing once a process works
questions.answer: Regularly reviewing and improving how services are delivered

title: Financial Regulations & Budget Discipline
objective: Ensure officers who handle funds understand the Financial Regulations, budget implementation and the controls that protect public money.
description: Covers the budget cycle, the Treasury Single Account, authorisation and payment controls, retirement of advances, and internal and external audit.

lessons.title: The Budget Cycle & Budget Discipline
lessons.description: The public budget moves through preparation, approval, implementation, and monitoring and evaluation. This lesson explains why spending must stay within appropriated amounts and approved budget lines.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of the budget cycle?
options: Preparation, approval, implementation, monitoring and evaluation
questions.answer: Preparation, approval, implementation, monitoring and evaluation

questions.question: Spending money on an item not in the approved budget without authorisation is...
options: Acceptable if the item is useful
questions.answer: A breach of budget discipline

questions.question: Why is budget monitoring important?
options: To compare actual spending with plans and correct deviations
questions.answer: To compare actual spending with plans and correct deviations

lessons.title: Treasury Single Account & Payment Controls
lessons.description: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) consolidates federal government revenues into one account at the Central Bank of Nigeria, improving visibility and control. This lesson also covers segregation of duties and approval levels for payments.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Treasury Single Account?
options: To consolidate government revenues into a single account at the Central Bank for better control
To allow each agency to open many commercial accounts
questions.answer: To consolidate government revenues into a single account at the Central Bank for better control

questions.question: Segregation of duties means...
options: No single officer controls all stages of a transaction
One officer approves, pays and records everything
Finance staff work in separate buildings
questions.answer: No single officer controls all stages of a transaction

questions.question: Before a payment is made, it should be...
options: Properly authorised, supported by documents and within budget
questions.answer: Properly authorised, supported by documents and within budget

lessons.title: Advances, Retirement & Audit
lessons.description: Cash advances must be retired promptly with receipts. This lesson covers retirement timelines, consequences of unretired advances, and how internal and external audit strengthen accountability.

questions.question: What does 'retiring an advance' mean?
options: Accounting for how the advance was spent, with receipts, and refunding any balance
Keeping the balance as a bonus
questions.answer: Accounting for how the advance was spent, with receipts, and refunding any balance

questions.question: What is the role of internal audit?
options: To independently review controls and compliance within the organisation
questions.answer: To independently review controls and compliance within the organisation

questions.question: Unretired advances can result in...
options: Recovery from salary and possible disciplinary action
questions.answer: Recovery from salary and possible disciplinary action
